$comment: MACHINE-READABLE REFERENCE — read this file to understand the `tlm` config block.
It defines every key a skill in this plugin may read: what it means, which skill consumes it,
whether it is a secret, and how the user obtains its value.
This file is DOCUMENTATION, not a live config. The live values live in the consuming
project's .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored). See ./settings.local.example.json
for a fillable template and ./SETUP-CHECKLIST.md for the walkthrough.
$changelogNote: Append an entry here — { version, summary, migration? } — every time a key under `tlm` is added, renamed, or changes meaning, and bump configVersion to match. hooks/setup-check.sh reads this to tell a teammate on an older schema exactly what's new; /project-setup reads it to know which fields to add on a sync run. `migration` is optional free text for anything not self-evident from the summary (e.g. a default to apply, or a value that must be re-asked).

holds: mcpServers — MCP server definitions, including any embedded API keys
tlm — this plugin's non-secret project config (the block described below)
primary.note: settings.local.json is the Claude Code convention for machine-local, gitignored config. Secrets MUST NOT go anywhere else in the repo.

holds: the `tlm` block only, as the file's root object
fallback.when: Use only if a Claude Code version rejects or strips the unknown `tlm` key from settings.local.json. Skills read settings.local.json first, then fall back to this file.

readOrder: 3. not found → tell the user to run /project-setup

mcpServers.$comment: Which MCP servers each capability needs, and when they are required.

context7.purpose: Fetch current library/framework/SDK documentation instead of relying on training data.

install.note: BUNDLED with the plugin (mcpServers in .claude-plugin/plugin.json) — loads automatically on install; do NOT add it to a project's settings.local.json. Requires Node for npx.

framelink-figma.purpose: Read Figma files/frames so a design can be turned into code.
framelink-figma.aka: This is THE way this plugin accesses Figma — the alternative to Claude's native/claude.ai 'Figma' connector. Use Framelink; do NOT enable the native Figma connector. 'Figma' words in a prompt trigger figma-to-code, which fetches through Framelink.
framelink-figma.detectBy: tool name matches mcp__*[Ff]ramelink* or mcp__*[Ff]igma*
framelink-figma.howToGetSecret: Figma → your avatar → Settings → Security → Personal access tokens → Generate new token. Scope: File content (read). Token looks like figd_xxxxxxxx.

install.note: BUNDLED with the plugin (mcpServers in plugin.json) — do NOT redefine it per project. The bundled server reads FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN from the project's env block; the ${FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN:-} default lets it start before the token is set. The ONLY per-project step is putting the token in env. NEVER paste a figd_ token into a committed file.

clickup.purpose: Read/update tickets, post comments, attach QA evidence.

install.steps: claude.ai → Settings → Connectors → ClickUp → Connect (OAuth). Then /mcp in Claude Code to confirm it is listed.
install.note: OAuth — no token is stored in settings.local.json. Only the non-secret workspaceId is.

jira.purpose: Same role as ClickUp for Jira-based projects.
jira.detectBy: tool name matches mcp__*[Aa]tlassian* or mcp__*jira*
jira.howToGetSecret: id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens → Create API token. Also needs the site URL (https://<org>.atlassian.net) and the account email.

linear.purpose: Same role as ClickUp for Linear-based projects.

install.command: claude mcp add --transport sse linear https://mcp.linear.app/sse
install.note: Authenticate in the browser when prompted.

github.purpose: GitHub Issues as the ticket system. No MCP needed — uses the gh CLI.

slack.purpose: Post the release note as a DRAFT to the release channel for a human to review and send.

install.steps: claude.ai → Settings → Connectors → Slack → Connect (OAuth). Then /mcp in Claude Code to confirm.

slack.note: Channel IDs are NOT secrets — they live in tlm.chat.channels.

$comment: AUTHORITATIVE list of the external dependencies ('companion plugins/tools') this plugin needs,
plus the ENFORCEMENT RULE. Required-by-capability:
1. The BASELINE is always expected.
2. A capability's companions are required ONLY when that capability is enabled — but then they
are REQUIRED, not best-effort.
3. A capability is ALL-OR-NOTHING: either enabled:true with every companion installed AND
verified with a real call, or enabled:false. There is no half-configured middle state.
4. A workflow skill MUST NOT run a half-configured capability. If a companion is missing, it
points the user at /project-setup to finish setup OR to set the capability's enabled:false,
then stops that skill. It does NOT limp along in a degraded 'local-only' mode.
5. Coding skills (fe-coding, rule-capture) have NO capability companions and always run.
This block documents CLIs (jq/node/gh/az/openspec) not covered under mcpServers; for MCP servers
it points back to the mcpServers entries above.

node.purpose: Runs the npx-based MCP servers (context7, Framelink) and the OpenSpec CLI.
node.minVersion: 18+ generally; >= 20.19.0 required if the spec-driven skill is used
node.install: https://nodejs.org, or a version manager (nvm / fnm / volta)

jq.purpose: Both hooks (SessionStart setup-check, PostToolUse lint-fe) parse their JSON payload with jq. Without jq BOTH hooks exit SILENTLY — no config warnings, no rule linting — and nothing tells the user enforcement is off. Treat as required.
jq.install: brew install jq (macOS) · apt install jq (Debian/Ubuntu) · choco install jq (Windows)

context7.purpose: Current library/framework docs. Expected for every skill.
context7.hardness: recommended — its absence downgrades doc-fetching but never blocks coding; still set it up as part of the baseline

design.hardness: HARD STOP — with the capability on but the design unfetchable, there is no reduced deliverable; the skill writes no UI code rather than guessing.

companions: the MCP/CLI for tlm.tickets.system — clickup | jira | linear | azure-devops (az) | github (gh)
tickets.hardness: REQUIRED — the skill blocks until the tracker is connected AND one real ticket verifies (name + status). If the user cannot connect it, they set tlm.tickets.enabled=false; the skill does not run in a degraded local-only mode.

chat.hardness: REQUIRED for the post step — the note text may still be produced, but posting blocks until Slack is connected and a draft verifies, or the user sets tlm.chat.enabled=false.

specDriven.enabledBy: tlm.specDriven.engine === 'openspec', or an openspec/ directory at the repo root
specDriven.requiredWhen: only when spec-driven work is opted into for a given ticket (per-ticket gate)
specDriven.hardness: DEGRADES — opt-in per ticket; if Node < 20.19 or npm is unreachable, fall back to ordinary fe-coding. Never a hard block.

tlm.$comment: Schema of the `tlm` block. Every leaf documents: what it is, who reads it, how to get it.

version.description: Schema version of this block. Bump when keys change meaning.

name.description: Human-readable project name. Used in release-note headings.

type.description: Which stack fe-coding applies. Also gates mobile-release-notes (mobile values only) and drives figma-to-code output style and deployment-checklist service mapping.

detect.nextjs-app-router: src/app/page.tsx or app/layout.tsx exists (UI in app/)
detect.nextjs-page-router: src/pages/_app.tsx exists; app/api/**/route.ts without app/page.tsx is Mode B of this, not App Router
detect.react-native-expo: package.json depends on expo AND expo-router
detect.react-native-cli: package.json depends on react-native without expo

type.note: fe-coding covers the four JS stacks. Flutter is recognized here only so mobile-release-notes can gate on it; there are no Flutter coding rules in ai/.

baseBranch.description: Branch new work is cut from and compared against.
baseBranch.source: auto-detect via `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, then confirm

apps.description: Monorepo only. Maps a path prefix to an app name, so release-notes can tell which app a commit range belongs to.

enabled.description: Does this project build screens from Figma designs? Gates the framelink MCP requirement.

mcp.description: Name of the MCP server entry in mcpServers that provides design access.

tokenEnvKey.description: Name of the env key in the `env` block holding the Figma token. The TOKEN ITSELF lives in `env`, never here.

enabled.description: Does this project track work in a ticket system? Gates ticket-workflow and the reconcile phase of deployment-checklist.

idPattern.description: Regex matching ticket ids in commit messages and branch names.
idPattern.source: auto-detect from git history, then confirm
idPattern.detectCommand: git log --oneline -80 | grep -oiE '[A-Z]{2,}-[0-9]+' | sed -E 's/-[0-9]+//' | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head

workspaceId.description: Workspace/team/site id, needed to build ticket URLs. ClickUp: the numeric id in any task URL. Jira: the site URL.
workspaceId.source: ask the user, or read from any ticket URL they paste

urlTemplate.description: Template for a ticket permalink. {id} is replaced with the ticket id.

inReview.description: Status set when work is submitted.

ready.description: Statuses that mean 'safe to ship'. Everything else is flagged in a release check.

statuses.source: fetch one real ticket with statuses expanded, show the user the real vocabulary, then ask

hasDeploymentTicket.description: Does the project use a single release/deployment ticket whose notes list what ships? Controls deployment-checklist PHASE 4.

planDir.description: Directory where ticket-workflow writes its per-ticket plan file (<planDir>/<TICKET>.md).

branchPrefixes.description: Maps a ticket's kind to the git branch prefix. Branch = <prefix>/<TICKET>-<kebab-summary>.

commentLanguage.description: Language for plan files and ticket comments, regardless of the chat language.

enabled.description: Does this project announce releases in a chat tool? Gates the Slack MCP requirement and the release-notes posting phase.

sendMode.description: ALWAYS prefer 'draft'. A draft lets a human review before it reaches an external/shared channel. 'send' requires explicit per-run user confirmation.

channels.description: Release channels. `app` matches a project.apps[].name so a monorepo posts to the right place.
channels.source: ask the user; the id is visible in Slack → channel → View channel details → bottom

mcp.description: MCP used to fetch up-to-date library docs. Always required.

specDriven.$comment: Spec-driven mode via OpenSpec (an external npm CLI, driven through npx — NOT an MCP). The spec-driven skill bootstraps it and drives its propose->apply->sync->archive loop. Detected by an openspec/ directory at the repo root; this block records the intent so the SessionStart hook can remind Claude.

engine.description: Spec engine for this project. 'openspec' means the spec-driven skill drives OpenSpec. Set once the repo is bootstrapped (openspec/ exists).
engine.source: set to 'openspec' after the spec-driven skill runs `npx openspec init`, or ask the user

mode.description: 'ask-per-ticket' — when a ticket or substantial feature starts, the skill ASKS whether to apply OpenSpec; only on yes does it run the OpenSpec loop, otherwise the normal rules skills run. Trivial fixes are never gated. 'off' — spec-driven suppressed even though openspec/ exists.

announceCommands.description: Print a one-line notice before running any openspec / npx openspec / /opsx:* command so the user is aware of what is triggered. Keep true — transparency is the trade for auto-driving.

detect.openspecDir: an openspec/ directory at the repo root (created by `openspec init`)

specDriven.requires: Node >= 20.19.0 for the OpenSpec CLI. Below that, or offline, the skill falls back to ordinary fe-coding.
specDriven.unifiesWith: tlm.tickets.planDir — when spec-driven is on, a ticket's OpenSpec change (openspec/changes/<ticket-id>-<slug>/) IS the plan; the ad-hoc plan file is not written.

$comment: CONTRIBUTE-BACK contract. The plugin installs read-only under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (a Claude Code
managed clone that /plugin marketplace update overwrites), so edits made there are lost and never
reach the team. This block lets a consuming project VENDOR the plugin's editable source into the
repo, edit it there, and open a PR upstream. rule-capture (plugin scope) and the vendor-watch hook
read this. Absent/enabled:false → the contribute-back flow is off and rule-capture only offers
project (CLAUDE.md) and memory scopes.

enabled.description: Does this project vendor the plugin source and allow opening PRs back to it? Set true by /project-setup when the user opts in.

upstreamRemote.description: Git push URL of the plugin's canonical upstream. A fresh checkout is cloned from here to build the PR branch — NEVER ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}.

ownerRepo.description: <owner>/<repo> on GitHub, used only to build the browser compare URL (https://github.com/<ownerRepo>/compare/...). Derived from upstreamRemote when omitted.

baseBranch.description: Branch on the upstream that rule PRs target and are cut from.

vendorDir.description: Path (repo-relative) of the committed, editable copy of the plugin's skills/ ai/ hooks/ setup/. NOT .claude/skills/ — that would double-register skill names against the installed plugin. The vendored copy is an EDIT + PR-STAGING surface only; edits do NOT take effect locally until merged upstream and pulled via /plugin marketplace update.

prMode.description: 'compare-url' — push the branch and print a GitHub compare link the user clicks to open the PR (no extra tooling). 'gh' — use the gh CLI to open the PR automatically (only if gh is installed and authed).

bump.description: Semver field the PR bumps in lockstep across plugin.json.version + marketplace.json metadata.version + plugins[0].version. A rule addition is a patch by default.

helperScript.description: The script rule-capture invokes to clone upstream, sync the vendored edits onto a branch, bump versions in lockstep, commit, push, and print the PR/compare URL. Read its header for the env vars it takes.

skillRequirements.$comment: Reverse index — what each skill needs before it can run. A skill MUST check this and, if something is missing, ask the user for it inline (during planning) rather than failing.

fe-coding.ifMissing: Auto-detect the stack from the repo, confirm with the user, then offer to persist it. Never blocks.

figma-to-code.ifMissing: HARD STOP — this is the one skill that must not degrade. If the Figma MCP is absent, unauthorized, or the fetch errors, report the specific failure and write NO UI code. Never approximate a design from a frame name, screenshot, or description: a guessed screen looks finished, so nobody re-checks it. Non-UI work in the same request may still proceed.

ticket-workflow.ifMissing: tickets is an all-or-nothing capability (see companions). If tlm.tickets.enabled is true, REQUIRE the tracker: ask for the system + id pattern inline, connect the MCP/CLI, and verify with one real ticket fetch (name + status) before continuing. If it cannot be connected now, do NOT run a degraded local-only mode — stop and offer two choices: finish setup via /project-setup, or set tlm.tickets.enabled=false to proceed without a tracker. Persist whatever is configured.

mobile-release-notes.ifMissing: chat is an all-or-nothing capability (see companions). If tlm.chat.enabled is true, the note text may still be produced, but the POST step REQUIRES Slack connected and a draft verified — do not skip silently. If Slack cannot be connected, stop at the post step and offer: finish setup via /project-setup, or set tlm.chat.enabled=false (produce the note for manual posting). If the project is web-only, stop and point at deployment-checklist instead.

config: tlm.pluginRepo (only for the PLUGIN scope / contribute-back path)
cli: git (always present); gh only if tlm.pluginRepo.prMode === 'gh'
rule-capture.ifMissing: Always runs — it has no capability companion. Reads ai/ and skills/ from the plugin, plus the project's CLAUDE.md and memory. The PLUGIN scope is the only part that needs setup: it edits the vendored copy (tlm.pluginRepo.vendorDir) and opens a PR upstream via plugin-pr.sh. If tlm.pluginRepo is absent or enabled:false, do NOT offer plugin scope — offer only project (CLAUDE.md) and memory scopes, and tell the user to run /project-setup if they want contribute-back. If git push fails (no upstream access), degrade: leave the branch/commit and tell the user how to push + open the PR by hand. Never edit ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in place — a marketplace update wipes it.

deployment-checklist.ifMissing: Falls back to its own PHASE 0 bootstrap.

spec-driven.ifMissing: No MCP or secret needed — OpenSpec is a CLI driven via npx. If openspec/ is absent, offer to bootstrap it (`npx openspec init --tools claude`). If Node < 20.19 or npm is unreachable, report it and fall back to ordinary fe-coding — never a hard stop. Applied per ticket only when the user agrees; otherwise the normal rules skills run.

rules: NEVER write a secret into any file that is not gitignored. settings.local.json only.
NEVER print a secret value back to the user or into a commit, comment, or log.

A capability is ALL-OR-NOTHING (see companions): if it is enabled, its companions are REQUIRED and verified before the owning skill runs; a missing companion stops that skill with two choices — finish setup via /project-setup, or set the capability enabled:false. No half-configured / degraded local-only mode.

Within an enabled capability, a still-missing VALUE (e.g. a channel id, a status name) is asked for INLINE during planning and persisted — the requirement is on the companion being connected+verified, not on drip-feeding every value up front.
The BASELINE (context7, jq, node) is expected in every project; jq and node absences are surfaced loudly because the hooks and npx-based servers silently no-op without them.
Coding skills (fe-coding, rule-capture) have no capability companions and always run, even with zero config.

At setup, DETECT the project's own rules/specs (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, .claude/rules, openspec/, docs/specs, eslint/prettier/biome/tsconfig) and HONOR them. The plugin's house rules layer on top and DEFER to an explicit project rule where they conflict — never silently override a documented project convention; surface the conflict and route a persistent override through rule-capture. Record the catalog in .claude/codebase-map.md.
After collecting a value at runtime, offer to persist it so the next run does not ask again.
Verify a newly configured integration with one real read (fetch a ticket, resolve a Figma file) before relying on it.

CONTRIBUTE-BACK: the plugin under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is a read-only managed clone — NEVER edit it in place to change a rule (a marketplace update overwrites it and the team never sees it). Persistent PLUGIN-scope rule changes go through the vendored copy (tlm.pluginRepo.vendorDir) + a PR to the upstream (plugin-pr.sh). The vendored copy is an EDIT/PR-STAGING surface, not a live override: a change takes effect only after the PR merges and the user runs /plugin marketplace update. It lives at .claude/tlm-plugin/, NOT .claude/skills/, so it does not double-register skills against the installed plugin.
